title: Foundry Hosted Agents: a framework-agnostic managed runtime for production agents, GA at end of June 2026
summary: The frontier-model news this week is mostly gated (GPT-5.6 is a ~20-partner limited preview, Gemini 3.5 Pro is still limited-preview), so the more adoptable development is a runtime, not a model. Microsoft Foundry's Hosted Agents (Foundry Agent Service) is a managed platform that runs your own agent code, packaged from any framework, on Microsoft-managed infrastructure, and Microsoft says it reaches General Availability by end of June 2026. As of run date 2026-06-29 it is live in public preview, callable today across 20 Azure regions; the Microsoft Learn concept page, updated 2026-06-25, still labels it 'currently in preview', so the honest framing is preview-now / GA-imminent, not GA-shipped. The core, dual-sourced fact is that this is a framework-agnostic managed agent runtime with stateful sandboxed sessions: the docs and the independent InfoQ write-up both describe managed sandboxed sessions with filesystem state and multiple-framework support exposing a stateful Responses API plus a lighter Invocations protocol. The Microsoft-stated specifics (single-org sourced across the Foundry blog and the Learn docs, not independently corroborated): each session runs in a per-session VM-isolated / hypervisor-isolated sandbox with a persistent $HOME filesystem and scale-to-zero stateful resume; every deployed agent is auto-assigned its own Microsoft Entra ID (agent identity) and endpoint at deploy time; and you deploy from source via azd without packaging a container. Docs-only operational numbers worth pinning: 15-minute idle timeout, 30-day maximum session lifetime, default quota of 50 concurrent active sessions per subscription per region, sandbox sizes of 0.5/1/2 vCPU, and a 20 GiB per-session disk budget with ~20 percent reserved for system use. The non-obvious so-what is the cost model: billing is per active session across CPU and memory, so the docs warn that oversizing 'multiplies cost by your concurrency' - the runtime is convenient, but right-sizing is now your job.
why_relevant: This is an AI-engineer-must-know because the agent stack is bifurcating into model + framework + runtime, and the runtime layer - where the agent actually executes, with isolation, identity, persisted state, and scaling - is becoming a managed product you can rent rather than hand-build. It is adoptable now (public preview, 20 regions) rather than gated like this week's GPT-5.6/Gemini previews, which is exactly the freshness-plus-usable axis that beats a preview-only model drop. The interesting tension to write to: it is genuinely framework-agnostic (Agent Framework, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, or custom Python/C# code) yet hard-wired to Azure and Microsoft Entra for identity, so the lock-in moves from your agent code to your runtime and IAM; and the per-session VM isolation with scale-to-zero is the real engineering substance, with a cost trap (per-session billing scales with concurrency) the marketing glosses over. It is distinct in kind and subject from every covered topic: it is not a protocol spec (MCP 2026-07-28 stateless revision), not a spec-driven workflow (GitHub Spec Kit), not an open-weight model (GLM-5.2, MiniMax-M3, DiffusionGemma), not a token-economy tool pair (RTK + Caveman), not a hosted single-purpose chat agent (Claude Tag in Slack), not an environment world model (Qwen-AgentWorld), and not a closed frontier agent model (Doubao Seed 2.1). None of the nine covers where and how an agent is hosted and executed in production, which is this brief's whole subject.
schema_facts: Vendor: Microsoft. Product: Hosted Agents in Foundry Agent Service (part of Microsoft Foundry, formerly Azure AI Foundry). Use these exact names; the platform-level product is 'Microsoft Foundry' and the service is 'Foundry Agent Service'. Status as of run date 2026-06-29: PUBLIC PREVIEW. The Microsoft Learn concept page (ms.date 2026-06-22, updated 2026-06-25) states verbatim 'Hosted agents are currently in preview.' The Foundry blog (BUILD 2026, published 2026-06-02) states the GA timeline as 'General Availability by end of June 2026'; do NOT assert it is already GA - frame as preview-now, GA-targeted-end-of-June-2026. Isolation: docs say 'Hosted agents run in per-session VM-isolated sandboxes'; the blog phrases the same thing as each session running in 'its own hypervisor-isolated sandbox with a dedicated persistent file system'. Persistent filesystem mounts are $HOME and /files. Identity: 'Every Hosted agent deployed to a Foundry project gets its own dedicated Microsoft Entra ID (agent identity) and dedicated endpoint - both created automatically at deploy time.' Deployment: source-code deploy via the azd tool (azd deploy / agent.yaml), container packaging optional, image pushed to Azure Container Registry. Languages: Python and C# (.NET) only; docs say 'You can use any agent framework - the protocol libraries are framework-agnostic.' Named supported frameworks (docs, primary-only): Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, or custom code. Protocols: Responses (OpenAI-compatible /responses contract), Invocations (arbitrary JSON), and Invocations (WebSocket, invocations_ws, preview, North Central US only); also Activity (Teams/M365) and A2A (preview). Region count: 20 Azure regions (the blog says 'across 20 Azure regions globally' and the docs list exactly 20). Operational numbers (DOCS-ONLY, single-sourced - cite as Microsoft-documented, not corroborated): idle timeout 15 minutes; session permanently deleted after 30 days of inactivity; default quota 50 maximum active concurrent sessions per subscription per region (adjustable via Microsoft Support); sandbox sizes 0.5 vCPU/1 GiB, 1 vCPU/2 GiB, 2 vCPU/4 GiB; per-session disk budget up to 20 GiB at 1 vCPU or larger with about 20 percent reserved for system use. Cost model (docs, verbatim sense): 'Billing is based on cpu + memory consumed across all active sessions' and 'oversizing multiplies cost by your concurrency'. Dated network note (docs): 'Foundry projects created after June 25, 2026 support a private (network-secured) Azure Container Registry'. SOURCING NOTE: the load-bearing dual-sourced fact (across the Microsoft docs AND the independent InfoQ write-up) is that this is a managed, framework-agnostic agent runtime with stateful sandboxed sessions exposing a Responses API plus an Invocations protocol. Everything else (Entra-per-agent, azd deploy, 20 regions, all the operational numbers, the GA date) is Microsoft-stated only (Foundry blog and/or Learn docs, same organization); attribute these as Microsoft-documented, never as independently corroborated. DO-NOT-INVENT list for the writer: no pricing figures or per-vCPU/per-GiB rates (the docs point to an external pricing page and give no rates); no benchmark scores or latency numbers (none are published for this service); no claim that it is generally available yet (it is preview as of 2026-06-29); no region count other than 20 and do not name a specific region as GA-only; no SDK/model-id strings beyond what is listed here; do not invent endpoint URLs beyond the path shapes documented; and do not tag or frame this as a Claude, GPT, OpenAI, Google, or LangGraph release - those names appear only as supported framework/SDK integrations or as comparison baselines (the gated GPT-5.6/Gemini previews), not as the subject of this brief.
